correctness.rationale: Orthogonal projector decomposition is exact for all r>=2 and all positive integer part sizes. Every cross-part RK4 entry is h phi(Nh)/24, every within-part off-diagonal equals h^2 q/24 times a quadratic with negative discriminant, and the diagonal is its same-part term plus strictly positive R(-qh). phi is strictly decreasing to minus infinity and has a unique positive root rho, establishing the sharp sign cutoff without reentry. The attained Laplacian eigenvalue N and R(-x)>0 show Euclidean contractivity has precisely the same cutoff. The standalone verification code confirms 512 exact direct matrices and critical symbolic identities; finite testing is not used as a universal argument.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The exact graph-specific threshold strictly exceeds the Euler guarantee; hence an Euler-based sufficient SSP theorem does not imply it. The general scalar spectral stability limit supplies a necessary spectral condition, not an entrywise sufficient one, as an explicitly calculated four-vertex path refutes that implication. Other generic universal positivity results do not establish this exact fixed-family endpoint conclusion.

originality.rationale: The classical RK4 scalar absolute-stability endpoint, generic SSP bounds, and complete-multipartite spectral structure are not asserted new. The claim is the strict all-partition exact endpoint positivity/stability equivalence and simultaneous cross-part sign transition. Compared proof implications against archival primary full texts, modern abstract-level related work, and public mathematical research records. A four-vertex path demonstrates why scalar spectral stability cannot alone imply entrywise positivity. Residual specialized-coverage and inaccessible full-text risks remain.

value.rationale: The theorem completely classifies endpoint positivity on the infinite family of all unweighted complete multipartite diffusion systems, a natural model of cross-community mixing. The universal rho/N cutoff is independent of partition sizes, exactly coincides with Euclidean RK4 spectral stability even though this equivalence fails on other graphs, strictly improves on forward Euler for every member, and identifies a precise artificial decoupling at the stability frontier. These structural phenomena supply robust benchmarks for high-order diffusion integrators and are not arbitrary finite recomputations.
